# GazeControl — Progress Board

Working memory for GazeControl (data-driven gaze control for virtual agents in a
triad conversation: two virtual agents + the user; gaze patterns collected before
turn-taking in real triad conversations drive the agents' gaze).

**Source of truth: this file.** `progress.html` is auto-generated from it on every
commit by the `progress-board` skill's pre-commit hook — never hand-edit the HTML.

Status legend: `[ ]` todo · `[~]` in progress · `[x]` done · `[!]` blocked.
Completed tasks carry a `_(done YYYY-MM-DD · <short-commit>)_` tag (the commit that
finished them, for history tracking); the dashboard keeps full detail for the most
recent few completed items and compacts older ones.

    - **The bag carries no UV mapping.** All 161 of its vertices (129 new ones plus the inner-lip rim that was merged into them) collapse onto UV (0, 0), so the whole cavity samples a single texel — the bottom-left corner of whichever albedo the agent wears. That corner is RGB(77, 85, 84) in the stock 4096² SMPL-X atlas (reads black) but RGB(245, 246, 241) in the 512² SMPLitex one, which is exactly why Agent A looked right and Agent B looked grey. Nothing else uses that texel: the nearest mapped UV is 0.029 away (15 px at 512², 120 px at 4096²).
    - `SmplxMouthInteriorSubmesh` (an `AssetPostprocessor`) moves every triangle whose three vertices all sit on UV (0, 0) — exactly 288 of the mesh's 21196 — onto submesh 1 and assigns `SMPLX-MouthInterior.mat` (URP Lit, base colour 0.055/0.02/0.02). There are no partially-mapped seam triangles, so the rule has no edge cases. Idempotent across reimports, and the scene needed no overrides: the second material slot is inherited from the model prefab.
    - **The FBX swap was a true drop-in.** Same node names (plus 15 unbound `*_end` leaf bones from Blender), same single source material, and the 520 blendshapes identical in name and order — so visemes stay at 506-519. Overwriting the asset in place kept its GUID, and both agents kept their materials, bone bindings and lipsync morph targets. Source vertices went 10475 → 10604; the file roughly doubled to 58 MB in LFS.

    - **The manual eye-disc composite is now a menu item**, `GazeControl → Textures → Composite SMPLitex Eye Disc`. SMPLitex never generates the eyeball island and leaves it black; both eyes share it, so an untreated texture gives black eyes. Pixels are read from the PNG rather than the imported texture, which is DXT1 — round-tripping through block compression to fix one disc would degrade the whole image. The (296, 221) r≈19 geometry from the 2026-07-26 note is **top-left origin**, confirmed by finding pure black there in the new textures and the composited disc there in the old one.
    - **`Pad SMPLitex UV Islands`** fills the gaps between islands from their edges, with the mesh's own UVs as the coverage mask, so nothing a triangle covers is ever written. It also repairs a flat background spilled *into* an island — but only when the background is measurably flat, which is checked rather than assumed (the modal outside-island colour must hold ≥50% of outside texels). It manages the FBX's Read/Write flag itself instead of leaving the project carrying it.
    - **Not fixed, and it is in the source:** `smplitex_f00016_alb.png` has yellow-green painted on the fingers and toes *inside* the islands. Three attempts to remove it failed on the same fact — there is no flat background to subtract. The modal outside-island colour is black at only **11.9%**, and the next seven (greys and pinks) each occur in 15k-43k *island* texels, so any colour rule that caught the green would eat real content. Reported rather than hand-tuned away; swapping the SMPLitex sample is the clean fix if it distracts.
    - `SMPLX.modelType` deliberately stays `Male`: it selects the betas-to-joints regressor, so it moves the skeleton rather than the mesh surface, and the FBX carries one template mesh. **The textures are female, the body is not** — that needs a female template export or non-zero betas.

  - [x] **Exported segment audio is peak-normalised, and baseline B was silently broken without it** — the corpus records at about **−42 dBFS**, so no frame ever reached the VAD's 0.01 RMS threshold and both agents sat on their fallback target (the user) for the entire take _(done 2026-08-10)_
    - Caught by the user watching the first takes and asking why the agents never look at each other. The gaze logs answered it immediately: **100% of baseline B's frames targeted the user**, which is precisely what "nobody is ever detected as speaking" looks like.
    - The exporter now peak-normalises to 0.70 with **one gain for both sides**, taken from the louder track (51.3× here). Per-track normalisation would rewrite the balance between the two speakers, which is recorded rather than incidental. Gain and pre-gain peak go into `segment.json`.
    - Checked the tracks really are speaker-separated before touching levels: during their own speaker's words each track carries **8-16× the energy** it does during the other's, and the two envelopes are anti-correlated (−0.16). Against the transcript, the normalised audio at the 0.01 threshold detects **86-89% of speech frames with 9-11% false positives on silence** — which is what the tracker's hysteresis exists to clean up.

  - [x] **Baseline A — Shintani et al. 2024 role-based gaze with aversion control** — `ShintaniGazePolicy` (semi-Markov dwell-and-shift) + `ShintaniGazeParameters` + `DeterministicRandom` (PCG32, one stream per agent) + `ConversationDirector`; wired as the `RoleConditioned` condition. 34 new tests, 48 green in `GazeControl.Gaze.Policy.Tests` _(done 2026-07-30)_
    - **Parameters are a committed config file**, `Assets/GazeControl/Resources/BaselineAParameters.json`, regenerated from the git-ignored corpus by `Tools/build_baseline_a_params.py`. That is what makes the condition reproducible on a clone without `Research/`.
    - Three departures from the paper, each forced by the corpus: **lognormal dwells** (χ² has no interior mode in 0 of 45 cells), the **jump chain** for target selection (i.i.d. draws from `S` would give person→person 0.35 against our measured 0.10), and an **empirical quantile table** for the aversion re-target interval (direction segments are clipped by their aversion, so a sixth fall below the 0.1 s fixation floor and the tail reaches 16 s — no two-parameter law covers both ends).
    - **No hand-written turn-boundary overrides** (user's call 2026-07-30). The `changing` half of the fitted parameters already carries the measured pre-turn effect, and a scripted yielding gaze in the baseline would pre-empt the proposed method's claim — which matters doubly because Baseline A is also the proposed method's substrate.
    - **No mutual-gaze breaking** either (same call): Shintani has no such term, and the 0.77-0.88 jump-to-aversion makes long lock-ins unlikely. `mutual_gaze_*` is still logged, so the assumption is checkable.
    - Personality/extraversion axis dropped (no NEO-FFI ratings, no GAR interpolation) — `S`/`L`/`D` collapse to one parameter set.
    - **Occupancy check**: a semi-Markov simulation of the committed parameters reproduces the corpus `S` to ≤0.046 absolute, worst cell `ad`/`holding`/gaze-at-speaker, where the fitted lognormal falls short of the empirical tail. The unit test asserts 0.06.
    - **Verified in Play Mode 2026-07-30**: roles resolve and persist through gaps (only the first 20 frames have no speaker), turn phases fire for exactly 1 s at each boundary, all 9 aversion directions appear, the eyes re-target inside a single aversion (t=3.33→3.47→3.60→3.87), eye pitch stays inside the corpus bins (−13.9°…+11.3°) and yaw inside the ±35° clamp.
    - Their §4.3 motion control (head ≤20°/s, eyes arrive first, blink above 40°) was **not** ported — it is a different animation layer from ours, and §0.1 requires one layer shared by all conditions.
    - `ConversationState.TimeSinceTurnStart` renamed **`TimeSinceTurnInstant`**: the corpus's `changing` window is centred on turn *instants*, so the gap after a turn ends is as close to one as the last second before it. Nothing read the old field.
  - [x] **Proposed method as a policy** — `ProposedGazePolicy` wraps a substrate policy and overrides it only inside the pre-turn window; `TriadConversation` no longer touches gaze at all. All three conditions now go through `IGazePolicy` onto one animation layer _(done 2026-08-02, substrate changed 2026-08-09)_
    - **The substrate is Baseline B (speaker-following) as of 2026-08-09**, not Baseline A — see Decisions. Taken as an `IGazePolicy` through the constructor, so swapping it is one line in the runner. The condition no longer loads the corpus parameters at all.
    - **Aversion rendering inside the window was reverted on 2026-08-02** (see Decisions): the prototypes' `None` recentres the eyes. With the Baseline B substrate this is now self-consistent — B never averts either, so the condition has no directional aversion anywhere. `AversionSampler` is reached only through `ShintaniGazePolicy`, i.e. Baseline A.
    - **The condition is fully deterministic.** Baseline B carries no random stream and the pattern draws none, so one recording *is* the condition rather than one draw from it. Confirmed empirically: two runs 17 minutes apart produced byte-identical gaze CSVs. The seed stays in the signature only so every condition is seeded and logged alike (§0.5).
    - The substrate is ticked **every** frame, including while the pattern overrides, so its hysteresis clocks follow the same trajectory whether or not a boundary is near. The window changes what is rendered, never what the substrate would have done.
    - The pattern now fires before **every** turn end, not just the A→B hand-over — that is what a policy does, and it means B's closing turn also carries the prototype. Retires the old "B engages A 0.8 s after turn onset" heuristic bridge, which only existed because there was no substrate to hand back to.
    - `GazePatterns`/`GazeRole` moved into the `GazeControl.Gaze.Policy` assembly (pure data, no Unity deps) — the policy assembly references nothing, so it could not otherwise see them. `PreTurnPattern`, `PreTurnWindowSeconds` and `PatternTimeScale` moved off `TriadConversation` onto the runner as `ProposedSettings`; the scene migrated with the same values.
    - **Verified against the substrate frame-by-frame 2026-08-09**: over one take the proposed condition differs from Baseline B in **14 of 354 frames**, in exactly two runs — `t=3.02-3.25` (A's turn end, current-speaker track) and `t=9.45-9.62` (B's turn end, next-speaker track). Every other frame is bit-identical. The contrast between the two conditions is now the pattern and nothing else.

Motivation: baseline B as substrate ignores the human user entirely between turns, while the corpus's holding-state ratios say real participants look at the side participant 13-23% of the time and avert 36-44%; and with sparse demo events, holding periods dominate the take. Framing: this becomes part of the proposed method (data-driven holding behaviour + EoT prototypes), not a tweak to a baseline; baselines A and B stay untouched, and a prototype-off ablation recovers the isolated pattern contrast if needed.
    - Plan approved 2026-08-14 (test-first workflow). Design points settled by the user: aversion renders as **recentred eyes** (consistent with the prototypes' `None`); on a role change the current fixation **finishes** (person remapped live), then a fresh stretch is drawn for the new role; draws are **per-agent** seeded streams (holding gaze is uncoordinated in the corpus); `ProposedSettings.Substrate` toggle (HoldingReplay default | SpeakerFollowing ablation). Bank: `Tools/build_holding_sequences.py` → committed `Assets/GazeControl/Resources/HoldingSequences.json`, ~250 stretches/role sampled deterministically from the 10,384 holding stretches the corpus yields.

At 250/role the worst cell sat 0.08 off the corpus S (the occupancy test asserts 0.06); at 500/role it is 0.028 with all nine cells inside. The full pool reproduces S to 4 decimals, so this is pure sampling variance, measured before choosing the size.

  - The runner logs forever once started; it should end the session when the conversation finishes. Harmless for a recorded take (the recorder exits Play Mode, so the 11.7 s takes give ~80 KB logs), but a free-running session still grows without bound.

## Decisions

- 2026-08-13 — **The Proposed condition's non-turn behaviour will be holding-period replay from our own corpus** (user's call, choosing between "tame baseline A" and "derive a non-turn model from our data"). Non-parametric replay was preferred over fitting a new parametric model: the event table tiles the timeline losslessly, so actual role-conditioned fixation sequences can be replayed verbatim — side-participant gaze and aversion time come out right by construction, with no dwell-law debate (chi-square and even lognormal fit these durations poorly). The reframe matters as much as the mechanism: the proposed method becomes *holding replay + EoT prototypes* as one full data-driven model, matching the project's ethos (corpus audio, corpus motion, corpus prototypes — now corpus sequences between them). **This will supersede the 2026-08-09 "substrate is baseline B" decision once implemented**; the isolated pattern-only contrast that decision bought is recovered by a prototype-off ablation, not by the substrate choice. Baselines A and B themselves stay untouched — a tuned baseline is not a baseline. Upstream data paths are now recorded in CLAUDE.md (Gaze control section).

- 2026-08-10 — **Case 1 replays a real TalkingWithHands conversation instead of a scripted TTS exchange** (user's call). The agents speak the corpus's own audio, move on its own mocap, and the gaze patterns fire on its annotated end-of-turn events. Kokoro TTS (`Assets/TTS/`, `KokoroTts`, `TtsSpeaker`) and `TriadConversation` are **deleted**, not left dormant — they were the only conversation source and dead code around a signed-off pipeline is worse than a git history lookup. What this buys the demo: real overlaps, backchannels and interruptions, boundaries that a human annotation pipeline found rather than ones we asserted, and a 24 s take with two hand-overs instead of a 12 s take with one.

- 2026-08-10 — **Every end-of-turn event fires a prototype drawn from its own class's pool** (user's call). All fifteen prototypes the paper prints are transcribed, so an interruption gets an interruption prototype and a turn-taking boundary gets a turn-taking one. Two consequences worth reporting: the proposed condition is no longer "one prototype, repeated", so a take exercises several of the paper's findings at once; and it is still fully deterministic, because the draw is a hash of the run's seed and the event index rather than a running random stream. **The pattern seed is the run's, not the agent's** — a per-agent seed would have each agent playing a different prototype's track at the other, which is the one way this could be quietly wrong.

- 2026-08-10 — **Segments are chosen by a documented, re-runnable filter rather than by eye.** `Tools/find_demo_segments.py` encodes what a usable demo segment is and ranks what survives. Two of its rules are worth keeping in mind when reading a take: utterances are rebuilt with the same 0.3 s pause split the event builder used, so segment boundaries agree with the events by construction; and backchannels are **not** dropped for boundary purposes even though the event builder drops them, because a boundary that cuts through "mm-hmm" still sounds like a cut.

- 2026-08-10 — **Exported segment audio is peak-normalised to 0.70, with one gain shared by both speakers.** The corpus records around −42 dBFS, far below anything the voice-activity detector's absolute-RMS threshold can see, so the raw levels made baseline B a constant stare at the human user. Normalising in the exporter rather than lowering the threshold fixes the demo's audibility at the same time and keeps the threshold calibrated in ordinary units. The gain is shared because the level difference between the two speakers is recorded, not incidental; it and the pre-gain peak are written into `segment.json` as provenance.

- 2026-08-10 (later) — **An agent speaking over the floor-holder addresses *them*, not the human.** This **supersedes** the fallback-to-human resolution adopted earlier the same day, which was correct that an agent is not its own addressee and wrong about where to send it instead. Talking while someone else holds the floor is what a backchannel is, so the case is common rather than exceptional, and the human fallback made an agent stare at the user for 66% of a take. §3's human fallback now applies only when neither `CurrentAddressee` nor `CurrentSpeaker` names anyone else. **Report baseline B as: look at the addressee, or at the floor-holder when the agent is talking over them.**
  - Worth remembering how it surfaced: the previous segment happened to have an agent that rarely backchannels, so the same bug cost 5% there and looked like rounding. Changing the material, not re-reading the code, is what exposed it.

- 2026-08-10 — **Speaker voice type is measured from the audio, because the corpus does not record it.** Median F0 per speaker over their own voiced frames, filterable as `--voice male|female|mixed`, stored in `segment.json`. Validated against a segment whose voices were known by ear. This is what makes "pick a two-male conversation" a query rather than a listening exercise, and it is what the agents' textures should be matched to.

- 2026-08-10 — **Baseline B's §3 rules now apply symmetrically to the agent itself.** Real conversation audio makes voice activity and the turn schedule disagree — backchannels, overlaps, early starts — and two gaps followed from that: `current_addressee` names whoever the *floor-holder* addresses, so it can name this agent (an agent is not its own addressee, and §3's fallback covers it); and backchannel suppression was applied only when switching *to* a partner, so the agent's own "yeah" still re-aimed it. Both are read out of §3 rather than invented, and neither could occur in the TTS demo where audio and schedule were the same thing. **Report baseline B as implementing §3's hysteresis uniformly across self and partners.**

- 2026-08-10 — **The recorded conversation runs on the frame clock, and that is a deliberate choice against the audio clock.** An audio-clock (`AudioSettings.dspTime`) version was implemented first, on the reasoning that a stalled player loop slides a frame-counted clock behind the voices — 3.5 s of divergence was measured in an editor session. It produced a take **0.7 s shorter than the segment with the last utterance clipped**, because Unity Recorder writes one output frame per rendered frame: the video's timeline *is* the frame count. Reverted. What was kept from the attempt: both voices are scheduled on a single DSP instant, and the conversation owns the one clock that motion, the turn schedule and every policy read.
  - The recorder also had to be made to **hold the segment until its encoder is up** (it clears its pending flag after `StartRecording`, and the conversation waits on that flag). Before this, the first **2.08 s** of the conversation was missing from every video — measured, not guessed, by cross-correlating the recorded audio against the source.

- 2026-08-09 — **The proposed method's substrate is Baseline B, not Baseline A** (user's call). **This reverses the 2026-07-27 decision.** Outside the pre-turn window the proposed agent is now bit-for-bit the speaker-following baseline, so the Proposed-vs-B contrast isolates the pattern exactly — measured at 14 differing frames out of 354. The trade is that Proposed-vs-A is no longer a controlled comparison but a comparison of two whole gaze models; **report the pairings accordingly**. Two things fall out of it: the condition has no directional aversion anywhere (B never averts, and the pattern's `None` recentres), which removes the mixed rendering the Baseline A substrate produced; and it is fully deterministic, since B carries no random stream.

- 2026-08-09 — **Each demo take gets one folder, `Recordings/<CaseName>/`, holding the videos *and* their gaze logs.** A video without its log cannot be traced back to the policy state that produced it, and keeping them in separate trees made that separation the default. `LogDirectory` is retired in favour of `OutputDirectory` + `CaseName`.

- 2026-08-02 — **No algorithm-driven body animation: the loaded mocap is used faithfully and gaze is eyes-only** (user's call). `GazeController.HeadContribution` goes to 0, retiring the fractional head turn. It was synthesising motion on top of the clip, and after `TriadConversation` froze the motion players it became the *only* thing moving — ±23° of head swing every half second on a still skeleton, which is the "head shaking" seen at the end of a take. The runner now also stops re-deciding gaze once the conversation has finished, so the tail is a still frame. **This supersedes the 2026-07-30 "HER 0.3 → 0.5" decision**, which came from Shintani 2025's finding that 0.3 reads introverted; report instead that head motion is mocap-only and identical across conditions, so §0.1 still holds.
  - The feared cost did not materialise: the ±35° eye clamp is reached 0 times during the conversation in all three conditions, and only in the frozen 1.5 s tail.

- 2026-08-02 — **Aversion re-targets on Shintani's 0.7 s constant, not the corpus's sampled interval** (user's call, after watching the first takes). This **supersedes the 2026-07-30 decision** to sample the empirical segment distribution. The measured median (0.217 s) produced thirteen direction changes inside one four-second aversion, which reads as darting; the corpus's own unbiased estimator says 0.939 s, and its segments come from an eye tracker at a finer grain than a gaze-shift annotation, so 0.217 s is the doubtful figure and 0.7 s sits inside the corpus's 0.6-0.94 s range. Report as the paper's constant, with our measurement noted.
  - Worth remembering how this was found: the complaint was about the *proposed method's* aversion, but the logs showed the offending episode was the shared Baseline A substrate, and the prototype's own avert segment was 0.28 s. Changing what was asked for would not have changed what was seen.

- 2026-08-02 (later) — **REVERSED: inside its pre-turn window the proposed condition recentres the eyes for `GazeRole.None`** instead of sampling a direction (user's call, asked twice). Outside the window its Baseline A substrate still averts directionally, so the condition renders "looking away" two different ways within a single take, and its aversion no longer matches Baseline A's. This is a known §0.1/§5.3 departure and **must be reported**: it is the one place the conditions differ in how gaze is rendered rather than in what is chosen. `AversionSampler` stays, reached through `ShintaniGazePolicy` only.

- 2026-08-02 — ~~**The proposed condition's aversion uses the same sampler as Baseline A**~~ (`AversionSampler`), not the old "recentre the eyes" rendering of `GazeRole.None` — superseded the same day, see above. The reasoning at the time: sharing the code made §0.1 true by construction rather than by discipline, and the alternative writes zeros into the log's aversion columns for one of the three conditions.

- 2026-08-02 — **The pre-turn pattern fires before every turn end**, not only the scripted A→B hand-over. A policy has no notion of "the interesting turn", and the paper's claim is about turn boundaries in general. Consequence: the demo now shows the prototype twice, including on B's closing turn.

- 2026-08-02 — **The mouth interior is real geometry separated by UV, not a blocker object.** The re-exported SMPL-X FBX carries a mouth bag, but it is unmapped — every one of its vertices sits on UV (0, 0) — so it rendered in whatever colour the agent's albedo happens to hold in its bottom-left texel: dark in the stock atlas, near-white in the SMPLitex one. Splitting those 288 triangles onto their own submesh at import time (`SmplxMouthInteriorSubmesh`) makes the cavity texture-independent, so any future SMPLitex agent gets a correct mouth for free. Chosen over splitting the material in Blender (a round trip per model revision) and over painting the texture corner dark (needs repeating for every new agent texture). The `MouthCavity`/`MouthBackdrop` blockers and their tuning menu are deleted.

- 2026-07-30 — **Baseline A is pure Shintani: no hand-authored turn-boundary overrides, no mutual-gaze breaking** (user's call). `baseline-spec.md` §2 prescribes both, but they belong to the superseded Mutlu/Goffman baseline. The `changing`/`holding` conditioning is the empirically-estimated version of the same effect, and a scripted turn-yielding gaze inside Baseline A would fire in exactly the window the proposed method overrides — contaminating the comparison and, since A is also the proposed method's substrate, both conditions at once. Mutual-gaze breaking is left out as one un-corpus-derived parameter that the measured 0.77-0.88 jump-to-aversion makes unnecessary; it stays checkable because `mutual_gaze_*` is logged.

- 2026-07-30 — **Baseline A's fitted parameters ship as a committed JSON config**, `Assets/GazeControl/Resources/BaselineAParameters.json`, generated by `Tools/build_baseline_a_params.py` from the git-ignored `Research/corpora`. Config over constants is what `baseline-spec.md` §2 asks for, and it means a fresh clone can run the condition without the corpus. The generator is committed so the numbers stay re-derivable.

- 2026-07-30 — **Aversion re-target intervals come from an empirical quantile table, not a fitted law.** Direction segments are clipped by the ends of their aversion, so 17% fall below the corpus's 0.1 s fixation floor while the tail reaches 16.6 s; a lognormal truncated at the floor would inflate the mean interval by about a quarter. The table spans p0-p99 (top 1% = 2.4-16.6 s truncated, and the governing aversion dwell truncates it in practice anyway). Only un-clipped segments are fitted, since the generator clips its own last segment the same way the corpus did.
  - The corpus README's 0.939 s re-targeting estimate (OLS of direction count on aversion duration) is **not** used: sampling intervals from the observed segment distribution reproduces the observed 2.12 directions per aversion by construction, whereas 0.939 s would give 1.8.

- 2026-07-13 — Gaze control and agent motion are both **data-driven**, from gaze behaviour patterns collected before turn-taking in real triad conversations.
- 2026-07-13 — Two target scenes: (1) A↔B turn-taking with the user watching; (2) agent A yields the turn to the user with gaze implication.

- 2026-07-13 — Triad layout: regular triangle, **side 1 m**, centered on world origin, everyone facing the centroid. Agents at (±0.5, 0, 0.2887); User at (0, 0, −0.5774) represented by the Main Camera at 1.6 m eye height under a `User` root.
- 2026-07-13 — Motion data format: **SMPL-X .npz** (TalkingWithHands): `poses` frames×165 axis-angle (55 joints), `trans`, 60 fps, Y-up right-handed, betas all zero. `*.npz` tracked via Git LFS.
- 2026-07-13 — Motion datasets stay **local-only**; git keeps just two whitelisted example clips (`…interloctr_000` + `…main-agent_000`, via LFS). New `.npz` under `Assets/MotionData/` is git-ignored unless whitelisted in `.gitignore`.
- 2026-07-13 — Clip pairing convention: the two agents always play a **matched take pair** — one plays the `interloctr` clip, the other the `main-agent` clip with the otherwise-identical file name (also in CLAUDE.md).
- 2026-07-13 — Triangle side length increased **1 m → 1.5 m** (agents at (±0.75, 0, 0.4330), user at (0, 0, −0.8660)).
- 2026-07-13 — Coordinate conversion: **direct axis-angle → Unity quaternion**, skipping 6D (that representation is for network regression, not playback). RH→LH mirror across the YZ plane: axis `(x,y,z)` → `(x,−y,−z)`, angle kept; positions `(x,y,z)` → `(−x,y,z)`. No up-axis correction needed (data already Y-up; the FBX pelvis parent chain −90°X·+90°X cancels).
- 2026-07-13 — Root translation applied **relative to the clip's first frame** by default, so agents stay anchored at their triad vertices (raw dataset positions available via a toggle on `SmplxMotionPlayer`).

Our custom code stays for what the package lacks: npz motion loading/playback and visemes. Its `QuatFromRodrigues` confirmed our axis-angle conversion is identical. License: research use, citation required; textures CC BY-NC.

Viseme map: Oculus `sil` → none, `PP…ou` → blendshapes 506–519; laughter target disabled. Editor `runInBackground` enabled so Play Mode advances while Unity is unfocused.

Model (~310 MB) + voice bins stay **out of git** (`Assets/Models/` ignored); README links the Hugging Face sources and an editor menu downloads them. Editor-only loading via AssetDatabase for now.

- 2026-07-13 — First gaze pattern: **Fig. 8d turn-taking prototype** from the ICMI paper ("current speaker glances at the next speaker twice" in the last second of the turn). Roles map to the demo as A = current speaker, B = next speaker, **user = listener** (camera plays the listener gaze track: steady on the speaker, then to B at the turn). Eyes do most of the gaze (35° clamp), head contributes a 0.3 fraction over the mocap pose.

- 2026-07-30 — **Q3 answered: sampled aversion in every condition**, including the proposed method. `GazeRole.None` stops recentering the eyes and becomes a sampled direction, so the animation layer is identical across conditions (§0.1, §5.3). This visibly changes the signed-off 7e demo — accepted. No guesswork needed: `aversion_direction/` gives 9-way marginals per role, the 9×9 first→second conditional, and **measured az/el per bin** (lateral ≈ ±20° yaw; up bins ≈ +11° pitch, down bins ≈ −13°), which land inside `baseline-spec.md` §1's guessed 15-30° / 10-20° band.
  - Re-targeting cadence: the corpus README claims 0.6-0.94 s "bracketing Shintani's 0.7 s", but `aversion_segments.csv` gives per-segment **median 0.22 s, mean 0.36 s** (2-3 segments per event, ~0.75 s mean aversion). Sample segment durations from the empirical distribution rather than any constant, which sidesteps the conflict.

- 2026-07-30 — **Q4 answered: minimal gaze-direction layer, no blink.** Body motion is pre-defined mocap from file, so the layer's only job is gaze direction. See the task entry for what is kept vs dropped.

- 2026-07-30 — **Corpus event table delivered and validated**, at `Research/corpora/` (git-ignored; regenerate from `F:\Code\scnpro\prototype\prototype`). It answers all three outstanding data questions and changes two plan assumptions:
  - **Use lognormal durations, not χ².** The corpus authors tested both: across role × target × `min_dwell`, **0 of 45 cells** give χ² an interior mode (fitted `dn` 0.88–1.78), and lognormal fits better in 8 of 9 cells (mean KS 0.051 vs 0.070). Shintani's χ² degenerates toward exponential on this data. This lands back on `baseline-spec.md` §2's original log-normal choice. Also: `dloc` is an artifact of the `min_dwell` filter (0.1 s), not a property of gaze.
  - **The "twitchy dwell" worry is resolved.** Real durations are roughly double the geometric ones implied by the transition matrix — mean 0.65–1.11 s, median 0.40–0.58 s, p90 1.3–2.5 s (vs 0.30–0.53 s geometric), with a genuine long tail. Gaze at the *speaker* is longest (~1.1 s), matching Shintani and Mutlu's ~0.98 s.
  - **`ad` is NOT an annotated addressee** — it is `second_speaker`, a hindsight label for whoever actually spoke next, which participants did not have at the time. `first_speaker[k] == second_speaker[k-1]` holds only **47.9%** of the time, so these do not form a floor-passing chain. `sp` is sound; `ad` is loose and `sd` inherits that looseness. Shintani's Addressee is a different variable — say so when reporting.
  - **Aversion direction was recovered** from the raw head-mounted eye tracker (34/38 sessions) rather than annotated: 9-way marginals per role plus the 9×9 first→second conditional. Measured re-targeting period 0.6–0.94 s **brackets Shintani's 0.7 s constant**. Note our distribution is flatter than theirs and lateral-down dominates (ld/rd ≈ 0.15) rather than pure down; `u` is rarest (0.05).
  - Other caveats from the corpus README worth carrying: `changing` covers 57.8% of gazed frames (dense turn annotation — narrow via `frames_to_turn` if needed); 24.26% of fixations outlive their governing event (`spans_events`); censoring is negligible (0.15%, drop it).

- 2026-07-27 — ~~**Baseline A supplies the proposed method's substrate**~~ — **superseded 2026-08-09, the substrate is now Baseline B; see above.** The reasoning at the time: outside the 1 s pre-turn window the proposed agent would *be* a Baseline A agent, isolating the contribution against A. Its consequence — that the transition matrix and dwell distributions sat on the critical path for two of three conditions — no longer holds; only Baseline A reads the corpus model now.

- 2026-07-27 — **Baseline A's parameters come from our own corpus**, not the literature table in `baseline.md` §2 — which is what that spec itself calls "strictly better". Source: `F:\Code\scnpro\prototype\prototype\output\transition_full_conv_legacymap\` (38 sessions, 2.0 M frames @ 60 fps). Two structural findings the literature guess misses: (a) **star topology** — leaving a person, ~90% of jumps go to aversion, not to the other person, so direct person→person shifts are rare; (b) our triad **averts far more** than the published proportions (speaker 0.445 vs 0.40, listener 0.397 vs 0.25, side participant 0.411 vs 0.25) and looks at the speaker much less (0.422 vs 0.65). EoT type (interruption/overlap/turn-taking) is irrelevant — max deviation from pooled is 0.0076, so use pooled.

- 2026-07-27 — The stored matrix is **per-frame at 60 Hz** (diagonals ~0.95), so Baseline A uses the derived **jump chain** (off-diagonals renormalised) plus separate dwell distributions. Reconstructing occupancy as `π·E[dwell]` normalised reproduces the observed occupancy to within 0.004 across all three roles, which validates the semi-Markov formulation — and removes the "solve for a matrix matching the §2 proportions" step from the plan entirely.

- 2026-07-27 — **Baseline B runs on the existing animation layer**; the §4 rewrite is a separate, later task. B uses person-targets only, so the rewrite buys it nothing, and changing `GazeController` would alter the appearance of the signed-off 7e demo unverified.

- 2026-07-27 — **Voice activity is measured from the clip waveform at the playback position**, not `AudioSource.GetOutputData` (which is distance-attenuated, so detection would depend on where the listener stands). When the audio engine's `timeSamples` is not advancing, an internal playback clock takes over — without that fallback a dead output device yields a complete, plausible-looking gaze log in which nobody ever speaks.

- 2026-07-27 — **Condition wiring lives in a menu command** (`GazeControl → Set Up Gaze Conditions`), not in the committed scene, while the scene carries in-flight MouthCavity edits. Note: Unity auto-saved the scene on entering Play Mode during testing, so the wiring had to be reverted by hand afterwards — expect this if you test the same way.

- 2026-07-26 — Agents get distinct appearances via **per-agent materials + SMPLitex SMPL-X textures**. SMPLitex outputs (512², no eyeball UV island) are used as-is for body/face; the eye disc is copied from the default 4096² SMPL-X albedo since both eyes share that single UV island. Agent A stays on the default `SMPLX-Male-URP`.
